programmes.d: Tracey Frame, 35, was convicted of killing David Nixon in April 2002 after he planned to end their relationship.
After 6-year-old Michelle Lee Dorr went missing, her father confessed to murdering her.

On a cold December night in 1993, Rose Larner stopped in a convenience store on her way to her boyfriend's house. She was never seen or heard from again. Rose's disappearance remained a mystery, until a tiny clue is found years later.
The 1996 investigation into 48-year-old Martha Hansen's murder is helped by a legal requirement.

A woman convicted of killing her mother in a car fire is granted a new trial. An expert witness has a different opinion as to how the fire started and, if proven, would clear the woman of any culpability.
The disappearance of a mail-order bride is suspicious when police learn of the husband's past wives.

When a policeman's house goes up in flames, experts suspect arson. The officer whose home was torched arrests low-level drug dealer James Wren, who confesses. But when the suspect vanishes, investigators question the authenticity of the confession.
A jeweler's search through old sales records helps police find likely suspects in a couple's murder.
Witnesses saw a woman in the back of a truck, flailing her arms and screaming. When they found a jacket near a pool of blood, they knew what they had seen wasn't a joy ride.
Garbage bag leads to a killer.
A college senior was found raped and murdered near an unpaved footpath used by students to walk from one side of campus to the other.
An investigation into the murder of Katie Poirier is stymied by the lack of a body.

A 29-year-old woman is killed instantly when a bomb explodes in her home. The device is so powerful that it embedded shrapnel in houses across the street. The bomber had not only knowledge and skill, but also a motive for murder.
The sensitive nose of a forensic examiner sniffs out murder.
The only clue recovered from a shooting is a twelve-guage shotgun. Scientists use unique methods to lift the serial number from the weapon to trace it to its owner
An assailant avoids the law for 16 years due to a lack of evidence.

A woman appears to have lost control of her SUV and plunged down an embankment into a shallow creek. But investigators suspect foul play when they find snowy footprints leading away from the crime scene.
The only clue recovered from a shooting is a twelve-guage shotgun.
In 2004, Mary Ann Clibbery was found brutally murdered at her Illinois business. Investigators had to determine if this was a robbery gone wrong or a calculated murder.
A serial arsonist starts several fires that cause the deaths of three people.

Fire engulfs the home where Lori Keidel and her siblings were left alone while their father went to the laundromat. Years after her mother's disappearance, Lori tells police she witnessed her mother's death.
Computers aid the police and FBI in solving a string of crimes in St. Louis.
A Colorado hunter is the victim of a well-planned crime. Investigators suspect two weapons and two killers. But forensic evidence points them in a different direction — one much closer to home.
Using an anonymous letter and geographical profiling, investigators close in on a serial rapist.
When a little girl got sick and died, investigators were stumped. Was it an accident, an unexplained illness or murder?
A three-year-old develops a respiratory condition. His father has Alzheimers.

A young hairdresser was sexually assaulted and murdered in her own beauty salon. The evidence at the crime scene didn't match any of the suspects and, after the initial investigation, the case went cold for ten years.
A murder investigation in Florida crosses jurisdictions from New York and Jamaica.

For seven years, a trio of men robbed one bank after another. They always got away before the police arrived and they left no evidence behind. But the way they stood and the clothes they wore told a story that could be read by forensic scientists.
An examination of the 2002 DC area shooting spree that resulted in ten murders.
A woman convicted of killing her mother in a car fire is granted a new trial.

No one in a quiet residential community saw anything unusual the day one of their neighbors was brutally attacked and murdered. Fingerprints found at the crime scene and surveillance video helped investigators to apprehend the presumed killer.
Notepad points to kidnapper.

In 1994, 19-year-old Shannon Melendi disappeared while at Emory University. Her disappearance remained a mystery for ten years, until new scientific testing cast a different light on Colvin "Butch" Hinton.
Debate over cause of death.

In 1981, 6-year-old Cassie Hansen disappeared from her Minnesota church during an evening service. After receiving a tip that an older man was seen carrying a small person, police found Cassie's body in a dumpster.
A killer leaves the scene with the genetic fingerprint of his victim.
In 2007, Shamaia Smith disappears from a strip club in East Hartford, CT. Police consider various patrons of the club, but focus on local businessman Kenneth Otto.
A vacuum-cleaner bag of microscopic paint-particles helps to identify a killer.
When a Native American woman is brutally killed in the desert of New Mexico, her killers leave a crime scene rich in forensic evidence: tire tracks, shoe impressions and even the murder weapons.
A mother of two vanishes after a shopping trip. Her body is discovered a month later.

The wife of an Air Force officer was found dead in her bed with a plastic laundry bag near her face. Further investigation proved that the scene had been staged. Her death wasn't an accident — it was cold-blooded murder.
A physics professor and NASA technology help to catch a killer.
In 2008, college co-ed Jenna Verhaalen was found dead in her Bryan, Texas apartment. Petechial hemorrhages in her eyes indicated that she was strangled.
In 1993, worldwide attention focused on robberies which targeted tourists in Florida.

In 1996, more than a dozen children in Seattle, Washington, were fighting for their lives. Each one of them had contracted a serious unknown illness. After one died, investigators knew the clock was ticking.
At a murder scene, investigators find a shoe-print, several foreign hairs and unknown fingerprints.
The body of 16-year-old Leanne Tiernan was discovered nine months after she disappeared. Forensic scientists found clues that painted a virtual portrait of her killer.
A death in Pennsylvania is strikingly similar to one in North Carolina.

Robert Sims returns home after working the night shift and finds his wife unconscious on the kitchen floor. Their son is fast asleep in an upstairs bedroom, but their six-week-old daughter, Heather, is missing.
A nurse learns that she has been deliberately infected with HIV.

In 1980, Michigan resident Shannon Mohr died in what her new husband, David Davis, reported to be a horseback riding accident. After her death, Shannon's family reported that Davis seemed far from grief-stricken.
A pregnant woman is found murdered in her air-conditioned bedroom.
In 2005, the body of young mother Summer Baldwin was found in a suitcase in a Texas landfill.
Police were puzzled by an obscure print found at a murder crime scene.

When a popular gym teacher is found dead of what appears to be an accidental gunshot wound, his family is suspicious. A tape recorded by the victim just before his death tells the true story of his strange marriage and his wife's insatiable greed.
A man is found dead in his home and his ex-wife has an almost perfect alibi.
Police are dispatched to the scene of a shooting and discover the victim's husband is one of their own: a homicide detective who says his wife accidentally shot herself in the head.
A union official is executed in his home not long after a strike by the union membership.
A serial arsonist starts several fires that cause millions of dollars worth of damage and the deaths of three people. He is discovered, partly through the use of forensic hypnosis.
Police use forensic evidence to re-examine the motives of a man who shot an intruder.
A police officer accused of killing his estranged wife insists she committed suicide.

A bomb, constructed to cause as much damage as possible, kills a victim with deadly force and flame. When a painstaking search yields some tiny clues, police are able to identify the killer as surely as if he'd signed them.
Clues at the scene of a possible murder-suicide lead investigators to believe otherwise.

On September 17, 1984, in a suburb of Tucson, Arizona, eight-year-old Vicki Hoskins left home on her pink bicycle to mail a letter for her mother. She never returned, but her slightly damaged bicycle was found nearby.
Two men were murdered and investigators find a link to an arson.

In the series premiere of "Forensic Files", the longest-running true crime series in history, a Connecticut flight attendant goes missing. Police suspect her husband is guilty of murder, but can they prove it?
With no forensic evidence inside a murder scene, investigators were baffled.

Police investigate a discarded sleeping bag containing bloody sneakers and a purse, which eventually leads to the body of a young woman. A mark found on the victim's body enables police to track the killer.
A search in Virginia's DNA databank reveals the identity of a news producer's murderer.

In 1991, San Francisco pornographer Artie Mitchell was murdered in his home. His brother and business partner, who was found near the scene carrying a rifle, later confesses to shooting Artie.The question is whether the shooting was premeditated.
Police investigate the shooting of a homicide detective's wife.
Responding to a 2008 garage fire, Illinois emergency response discovered a man crushed beneath a truck.
A woman dies after a long search for medical help in dealing with the side effects of lithium.
In 1962, the small town residents of Hanford, California lost their sense of peace when one of their own, 15-year-old Marlene Miller, was murdered.
A woman is found dead in a ravine, but crucial crime scene evidence had been washed away by storms.
The victim was a self-made man who never minced words. Perhaps he was murdered by a disgruntled client or employee. Perhaps the racy photos in his safe held the clue to solving the crime.
An 11-year-old girl is sexually assaulted and shot twice at close range.

When the head chef of a historic Philadelphia restaurant was found dead, investigators interviewed the usual suspects: family, friends and coworkers. As they sifted through the evidence, police uncovered a chilling tale of debt and deceit.
A woman is killed weeks before testifying against the man who sexually assaulted her.
The bodies of several women are found on a remote hill in California. The police get a break when a prostitute escapes and is able to identify her attacker and his automobile.
New York police hunt the Zodiac killer after a series of deadly attacks.
Paul Gruber's daughter suspected something was wrong when she received birthday cards addressed from her father, but written in a stranger's handwriting.
A healthy man dies mysteriously in his sleep and toxicology tests reveal a lethal dose of lidocaine.
Armed with little else, police hoped that shoe impressions found at a Lansing, Michigan crime scene would put their investigation of Audrey Nichols' murder back on track.
A woman's diary helps police piece together the events surrounding her murder.
In 1996, Virginia Beach police arrive at the Makdessi apartment to find the bloodied bodies of Elise Makdessi and Navy sailor Quincy Brown. But was Brown Elise's lover or her assailant?
When a retired police officer is discovered murdered in his bed, his wife claims it's suicide.
In this classic episode of Forensic Files, the longest-running true crime series in television history, a serial bomber targets a judge, two attorneys and even a courthouse.
A suspicious fire swept through an apartment killing two young women.
In 1999, 9-year-old Valiree Jackson vanished on her way to school near Spokane. Her father, Brad Jackson, reported the disappearance and the entire community started searching for her abductor.
When anomalies stall a murder case, a candy wrapper and seeds help expose the killer.
When a young girl was found dead, police quickly arrested the most likely suspect. But cutting-edge technology from NASA enabled a forensic odontologist to prove the wrong man was behind bars.
The body of a Connecticut man is found in a burning rental car in Mexico.
In 2008, the body of Colorado real estate developer Alan Helmick was found by his wife, Miriam, who then became the prime suspect.
When a pipe bomb ripped through a rural home, police had no idea who was responsible.
When Chris Ochoa confessed to the 1988 rape and murder of Nancy DePriest, the case was closed. 8 years later, Achim Marino confessed to the same crime. Can DNA evidence identify the real perpetrator?
Fingerprints found at the crime scene helped investigators to apprehend a killer.
